texto: c’est un film très lent, avec une atmosphère étrange et de très très très très longs dialogues. c’est un infini procès, avec une embrouille interminable, qui révèle une ambiance très sombre et des personnages tous plus bizarres les uns que les autres. on comprend pas tout et c’est très compliqué d’accrocher. certains plans sont filmées de façon original, et les scènes sont vraiment longues. c’est un film chargé en émotion, avec beaucoup de secrets enfouies. au bout d’un moment ça devient vraiment interminable, des faits surgissent, des hypothèses sont conjecturées, mais c’est jamais explicitement concret. bon ok la façon dont c’est réalisé est très intéressante. par contre, j’ai carrément détesté la fin, pcq tout le long on s’attend à une réponse concrète mais le but du film c’est justement de ne donner aucune réponse, du coup c’est super frustrant. toute l’histoire on peut l’interpréter seulement par des « peut être » et jamais par de véritables faits. chacun des personnages sont intéressants, avec des points de vus différents et des façons de subir la situation différentes, mais le spectateur est à la place des jurés, donc c’est très compliqué de savoir démêlé le vrai du faux. le film rappelle que le verdict ne coïncide pas forcément avec la vérité, et les hypothèses de la potentielle vérité restent plausible. cependant le lien avec le titre du film est très pertinent, en montrant la chute de chacun des personnages de façon disséquées. bon, en toute honnêteté je n’ai pas aimé. le fond du film est émouvant et bien recherché. MAIS, c’est lent + dialogues interminables + bcp de choses abstraites et surtout surtout surtout le film répond à rien, ça te laisse sur ta fin, c’est à toi d’interpréter et de trouver la vérité, la fin est ouverte et ne répond à aucune questions que tu te poses durant tout le film. c’est frustrant et c’est carrément ce que je n’aime pas.

texto: DE // ENG Ein Film für Fans von Kriminalfällen. Man kann schön mitraten, interpretieren und Hypothesen aufstellen. Man bekommt auch genügend Zeit dafür. Denn manche Gespräche sind lang und manche Einstellungen länger. Für mich hat sich das alles etwas zu sehr gezogen und endet unzufriedenstellend. Aber ich hatte mir schon gedacht, dass es so endet, da es zum Vibe des Filmes passt. Kommt selten vor, dass ich mit der Allgemeinen Meinung über einen Film so weit auseinander gehe. Ich stelle immer wieder fest, Krimi gehört nicht zu meinen favoritisierten Genres. // A movie for fans of crime mysteries. It’s fun to try to figure things out, interpret what’s happening, and come up with theories. You’re given plenty of time to do so, too, since some conversations are long and some shots are even longer. For me, it all dragged on a bit too much and ended unsatisfactorily. But I had already suspected it would end that way, since it fits the vibe of the movie. It’s rare for me to disagree so strongly with the general consensus on a movie. I keep realizing that crime thrillers aren’t among my favorite genres.

texto: Me  pareció una película muy interesante. Desde el principio logró mantener mi atención, pero lo que más me gustó fue la actuación de Sandra Hüller. El hecho de que hable inglés, francés y alemán hace que su personaje tenga mucho más carácter y se sienta muy real, su personaje muestra inteligencia pero sabemos que es la actriz dándole vida y eso me encanta. Para mí, la película es una mezcla entre una historia fácil de seguir y el cine de arte. Aunque trata de un juicio, no solo busca resolver el caso, sino que te hace pensar en todo lo que pasa y en cómo cada persona puede ver la misma situación de una forma diferente. Al final, porque no te dice exactamente qué pasó. En lugar de darte una respuesta, deja que cada espectador saque sus propias conclusiones con las pruebas que fueron apareciendo durante la película.

Best Criterion purchase I made since Memories of Murder . ________________________________________________________ Anatomy of a Fall enticed me from the premise alone. A woman is blamed for her husband’s death and the only witness is her blind son. That in it of itself is enough to get my attention. The film is an amazing courtroom drama. It’s similar to A Few Good Men in that every single court sequence is riveting, filled with incredible dialogue and tense confrontations. The movie does a great job creating suspense and tension. I genuinely did not know how it was all gonna play out. What makes this movie stand out though is at its heart, it’s a family drama. It’s about a marriage on the brink of collapse, and how the couple’s issues are impacting their loved ones. It tackles very real topics like infidelity, sexuality, childhood, abuse, depression, and grief. I found myself caring about these characters and the struggles they endured throughout the movie’s runtime. Everything about this movie felt real. Never once did I feel like I was watching a movie. Anatomy of a Fall felt more like someone hid a camera inside someone’s house rather than actors reciting lines from a script (a very well written script I might add) in front of a camera. The authenticity of this film is thanks equally to the screen writer(s) and the actors. Sandra Hüller in particular is downright incredible. The realism of this movie is a bit of a blessing and a curse. I love that the director allowed certain scenes to “breathe.” It created a bunch of heartfelt moments and it gives the viewer the chance to sit with these characters and empathize with them. That being said, I felt like some scenes dragged on for a little too long, and it ruined the pacing in some parts. But once again, maybe on second watch, I’ll feel differently. Bottom line, I love Anatomy of a Fall . I can’t wait to watch it again. In fact I kinda have to watch it again. I watched it while my wife was at book club. When she returned and realized I was watching this movie, she was like “OMG I wanted to watch that too!” Sorry babe. 😜

texto: Palme d’or 2023 et couronné de nombreuses récompenses, Anatomie d’une chute de Justine Triet mérite largement sa réputation. Derrière son apparence de film judiciaire se cache avant tout une dissection fascinante d’un couple en crise, où chaque détail du quotidien prend une importance capitale. Le suspense autour de ce whodunit atypique fonctionne parfaitement, mais le véritable sujet est ailleurs : les ressentis, les incompréhensions et les visions opposées que deux personnes peuvent avoir d’une même histoire. Sandra Hüller livre une prestation remarquable, parvenant à transmettre une multitude d’émotions d’un simple regard. Une réalisation subtile qui nous plonge au plus près des émotions des personnages. Un très bon film.

texto: I love movies like this, especially the legal aspect. It’s even better when a film manages to make it feel tense and gripping. The various camera angles and shots were well executed. The plot was greatly enhanced by the atmosphere, the music, and—above all—the characters. I found the acting to be very strong; the lawyer, the mother, the son, and especially the dog all mastered their roles brilliantly. The dog deserves an award! At times during the movie, I genuinely thought the boy was blind in real life (i.e., outside the context of the film). A very convincing performance. As mentioned, the courtroom scenes were a highlight for me, and I found the ending very powerful, too. It evoked a feeling similar to the movie *The Hunt*; the viewing experience felt stark and devoid of the usual clichés. In my opinion, the ending made the most of the situation—even if that statement sounds ironic. Fortunately, the instrumental version of 50 Cent’s "P.I.M.P." was used instead of "Jolene," which had originally been planned; "P.I.M.P." fit the content perfectly.

texto: Mettez du respect et de la lumière sur le cinéma féminin. Un film de procès qui ne cherche jamais vraiment le verdict, mais la faille. Triet construit son récit comme une dissection minutieuse du couple, où chaque certitude s'effrite à mesure que le tribunal (et le spectateur) croit avancer. Sandra Hüller y est habitée d'une opacité fascinante : on ne sait jamais si son intelligence est une armure ou un aveu. Mais au-delà du dispositif judiciaire, c'est une question bien plus vertigineuse que pose le film : connaît-on vraiment l'autre ? Son voisin, son frère, sa sœur, son ou sa compagne ? Aucune famille n'échappe aux secrets de polichinelle, à ces zones d'ombre qui persistent sans jamais être nommées. Chaque foyer a ses casseroles, ses non-dits tolérés en silence. C'est ce qui rend le film aussi dramatique que profondément humain. Il ne s'agit pas de juger un couple, mais de mesurer combien la connaissance intime de l'autre [ et de soi-même ] reste toujours partielle, négociée, parfois illusoire. Une leçon d'humilité face à la complexité des êtres. La mise en scène, souvent austère, presque clinique, épouse cette froideur alpine du chalet, comme si le décor lui-même refusait de trancher. C'est là toute l'ambiguïté du film : il ne raconte pas une mort mais l'impossibilité de connaître véritablement l'autre même après des années de vie commune. Les 2h30 pèsent par moments, notamment dans les longueurs procédurales qui, même si elles nourrissent le vertige du doute, testent aussi la patience. L'usage de l'anglais, pivot thématique plus que coquetterie, dérange certains. J'avoue que j'ai eu du mal avec ce yoyo entre les langues mais c'est à tort selon moi, tant il matérialise la distance entre les langues, les cultures, et finalement entre les personnes elles-mêmes. Une Palme d'or qui ne fait pas l'unanimité, et c'est peut-être normal. le film refuse lui-même toute unanimité sur ce qu'il raconte comme il refuse toute certitude sur ceux qu'on croit connaître. Pas le meilleur rythme mais très bon film.

texto: Jour 12 pour voir le top 100 Letterboxd Dans un pays imaginaire, après une guerre de religion, les enfant d'une mère ayant vécu ce fameux conflit tente de retrouver leur père et leur frère caché. Ce film aurait pu montrer les horreurs commises dans les deux camps, tout en mettant en évidence l'absurdité de ces conflits et de la haine qu'ils engendrent. MAIS… Il ne faut visiblement pas brusquer le monde du cinéma. Alors, plutôt que de mettre les deux camps sur un pied d'égalité, on va s'attaquer à ceux qui ne disent rien. Je vous laisse deviner ? ( NON ) Les Chrétiens. On a donc un film qui imagine un pays, qui suggère l'appartenance musulman de l'un des camps ( Clairement inspiré du Liban) mais qui, pour l'autre, n'hésite pas à multiplier les références chrétiennes : la Vierge Marie sur AK47 après avoir abatue de sangfroig un bus entier d'innocent, des croix montrées à plusieurs reprises, des discours chrétiens entre deux scènes de torture, etc. Alors oui, le film montre des atrocités commises par différents camp. Mais pourquoi insister autant sur l'iconographie chrétienne lorsqu'il s'agit de représenter la violence ? à force, cela mes un noms simple a retenir sur ces atrocité " Le christianisme ". Et c'est justement ce qui me dérange : si le but était de dénoncer les horreurs d'une guerre de religion, pourquoi ne pas donner la même place aux symboles et à l'identité religieuse des deux camps ? Pour votre gouverne, 4849 chrétiens ont été tués dans le monde en 2026, dont 93% en afrique, selon les chiffres d'Open Doors. Ce film aurait dû faire beaucoup plus de bruit. Edit : 4800 comme le nombre de personne qui on mis 2 etoile a ce film ;)

MAIS… Il ne faut visiblement pas brusquer le monde du cinéma. Alors, plutôt que de mettre les deux camps sur un pied d'égalité, on va s'attaquer à ceux qui ne disent rien. Je vous laisse deviner ? ( NON ) Les Chrétiens. On a donc un film qui imagine un pays, qui suggère l'appartenance musulman de l'un des camps ( Clairement inspiré du Liban) mais qui, pour l'autre, n'hésite pas à multiplier les références chrétiennes : la Vierge Marie sur AK47 après avoir abatue de sangfroig un bus entier d'innocent, des croix montrées à plusieurs reprises, des discours chrétiens entre deux scènes de torture, etc. Alors oui, le film montre des atrocités commises par différents camp. Mais pourquoi insister autant sur l'iconographie chrétienne lorsqu'il s'agit de représenter la violence ? à force, cela mes un noms simple a retenir sur ces atrocité " Le christianisme ". Et c'est justement ce qui me dérange : si le but était de dénoncer les horreurs d'une guerre de religion, pourquoi ne pas donner la même place aux symboles et à l'identité religieuse des deux camps ? Pour votre gouverne, 4849 chrétiens ont été tués dans le monde en 2026, dont 93% en afrique, selon les chiffres d'Open Doors. Ce film aurait dû faire beaucoup plus de bruit. Edit : 4800 comme le nombre de personne qui on mis 2 etoile a ce film ;)

texto: Um filme COVARDE Na sua busca do choque pelo choque, é o que Villeneuve se propôs aqui. Sua visão estéril sobre um filme, que por escolha própria, quis se ambientar em um local recheado de complexidade há 1000 anos, é pobre, rasa, fraca. O medo de entrar 1% na política fez o filme caminhar sobre uma pilha de coincidências até desembocar no "ápice" do filme. O fundamentalismo religioso é o cerne da violência que separa filho da mãe, que acaba com vilarejos milenares, que est*** mulheres e crianças com mais ódio e crueldade por volta dos anos 50', no oriente médio, isso não podia ser tocado no filme, porque implicaria culpa ao ocidente e Denis não tem essa coragem. O dito só precisa da locação, da língua e do povo, para que o OCIDENTE asissti-se aquilo tudo como - CENÁRIO - aonde se passa a tragédia e logo conectasse o pensamento com o que fomos ensinados sobre qualquer lugar do Oriente Médio: SÃO BÁRBAROS, POVO AMALDIÇOADO POR DEUS. Então a covardia, o medo, seu tom pasteurizado e apolítico construiu Incêndios, um filme covarde que busca o choque pelo choque, que o trauma é só uma escada pra te tirar um "NOSSA" no final. O filme é tão pobre é recheado de fatias de nada com coisa nenhuma, que se você reassiste, caso você tenha interesse (acho muito improvável), ele fica NADA. O filme poderia ter se passado em qualquer lugar, em qualquer época, é tão genérico, tão desconectado de tudo, que tanto faz se se passa em Ourinhos, Hamburgo, Xangai, New Jersey, tanto faz. Ele é neutro, ele apolitico, ele é covarde (de novo, muito covarde), o choque pelo choque, tudo pelo seu final, que nem é tão chocante assim. Um filme sem nuance, sem brio, sem força, sem alma

texto: I am so very split on this movie. On the one hand, it brought me to tears, it is empathetic, it is beautifully shot. On the other, it is exploitative, ignorant, reductive. It presents one of the most violent, most disturbing, most saddening scenes and then undermines itself by needledropping a Radiohead song, playing it as safe as imaginable for a presumably western audience. Throughout the movie I was wondering, what country is this even about? I thought I missed an explanation and was trying to connect the dots, people speak Arabic, there is some kind of civil conflict in the 70s and 80s, there is a "Christian right" in conflict with a presumed (is it ever even made explicit?) left resistance. Why not make explicit that this is about the civil war in Lebanon? Clearly, the movie's relation to politics is as timid as Villeneuve's early attempts at making the landscape a character, conveying emotion purely through filming these very wide shots, but it always draws back before really going anywhere, seemingly afraid it would offend an audience's sensibilities. If the central hypothesis of Deleuze and Guattari needed any more confirmation, it is here that we find it: The main character's real life inspiration (Soha Bechara) was a communist soldier, the assassination attempt that landed her in prison was committed on a reactionary South Lebanese army general. But the movie stays fundamentally incurious about her motivations, about the motivations of the Lebanese armed forces, it has no interest understanding how people get so racist they commit these atrocities and it is especially afraid to be seen "taking a side". What the movie instead opts to do is write an oedipal drama; it is all about *family*. Politics, religion, personal convictions, historical situations, they all collapse into a backdrop to what really matters: Love, trauma, anger, all happening within the theatre of the oedipal triangle, mommy - daddy - me. I can't deny that said oedipal story did work on me and hit me emotionally, even more though I think it is a real shame how close this actually gets to being earnestly good and thoughtful. It wouldn't have needed much, all it would take is that this movie is less afraid of "politics", of "taking sides" and that it dares actually embrace a perspective on something instead of avoiding that by any means necessary.

texto: Butchered arabic, dialects that have nothing to do with the region (the militia chief is Moroccan, they couldn’t go furthest than that). Plus it doesn’t make sense, the kid grows up in a Christian orphanage then gets recruited in a “Muslim” organization, starts killing Christian militia fighters, the day he gets captured he kills seven of them but they keep him alive and even give him a position in their ranks. And to make it even worse he starts torturing the people that were in his faction. Not to mention that the main character begins searching for her lost son only when the civil war starts. What about doing it before? It clearly doesn’t make sense. Also they make it as the refugees were the problem and not the Israeli interference in Lebanon’s politics.

texto: ????????? The “gotchya” here being incestuous rape is so insane when the viewer would literally have NO WAY of putting it together because they used the same actor to depict a 15 year old and a 40 year old. There is no possible way the viewer can suspend their belief when the person we see commit the violence to The Woman Who Sings is LITERALLY A GROWN 36 YEAR OLD MAN. i just feel like i’ve had a really bad magic trick done in front of me that took 2 and a half hours of my life. I was actually really into this at first. I could feel some form of the twist burgeoning from the beginning of the second act, but actually just wtf???? It’s not even a “gotchya” it’s more of if they’d simply casted someone who even slightly resembled a young man or teenager I would have been able to make the connection without being explicitly told. The entire plots crumbles into nothing here. Look, the film was shot beautifully. Like I said i was invested, but In the end we have a lukewarm apolitical take that uses Arab lives as collateral for some “family is One” “Love thy neighbor as your brother” shit. Complete ignorance of the ACTUAL conflict that took place & is purposefully obtuse regarding the violence that was literally and TRUTHFULLY committed by Israel. I’m really really really not usually bothered by casting that may or may not be the “obvious” choice but the casting here literally obliterates this film. Nothing makes sense by the end of it. Hands down least favorite Villeneuve film I have seen. Still seated for Dune 3 but girrrrllll u pissed me clean tf off with this one.

texto: 該怎麼說呢，火燒車與結局確實震撼，但整體敘事卻感覺綁手綁腳，沒能更好地用鏡頭傳達，但也確實讓我很好奇原劇作的呈現，應該會比電影精彩很多吧？ 本片多次在觀眾試圖解讀影像之前率先透過某人講出媽媽發生什麼事，忽然失去探索影像的主導權，身為電影觀眾不免對此有些反感，且講完了還要再給你看事發當下的鏡頭，感到多餘的同時馬上瞭然不過是因為劊子手的臉很重要，觀眾要先看到他，後面才能產生劇本想要的震撼效果，但這種目的性極強的鏡頭手法卻讓人有點難以忍受。 火燒車那場戲的震撼度仍然是全場最佳，也確實帶出極有說服力的轉捩點，但下一幕就接到另一個時空女兒來到媽媽家鄉悠閒散步的觀光客模樣，又讓我惋愕怎麼能就此放掉火燒車場面的後座力，轉而把觀眾的情緒切斷？ 而全片都在用這種七零八落的平行敘事，看完後除了瞭解事態全貌與結局的震撼感外，在反思層面與鏡頭語言上卻蒼白得嚇人，無從得知媽媽後來是怎麼克服仇恨與兩個小孩相處的？知道真相後的媽媽是如何從震撼掙扎到寫出那兩封信的？小兒子是帶著怎樣的心情與思考後不小心脫口而出「畢竟我有那種基因」的？ 總之本片拋出了極其龐大的議題卻在影像上處理得零零落落、捉襟見肘，身為觀眾都不免為導演緊張得要命，也搞得「1+1=1」這種台詞像是用完即棄的震撼彈，炸完了什麼也沒能留下。

texto: I wasn’t a huge fan of this one. There were too many plot points that just didn’t make sense to me, so I personally think it’s pretty overrated. That being said, the music is incredible. Opening the film with Radiohead’s You and Whose Army immediately gave me goosebumps, and the performances were also really strong. My main issue is still the writing. There are too many things in the plot that I just can’t make sense of, and at times it feels like the movie is trying too hard to make the audience suffer just for the sake of tragedy. It uses an extreme family tragedy to reflect on religion and war, but overall I found the film very heavy and slow

texto: Fui assistir esse filme pq sempre aparecia pra mim em recomendações de filmes com os plot twists mais absurdos. So que eu mesmo estraguei a experiência desse filme pq previ o plot final no meio do filme, na vdd, eu chutei qual seria o plot, pq eu tinha dado uma ideia muito viajada, só que no final das contas, realmente foi o plot do filme. Mas mesmo sabendo do plot, ainda teve um impacto em mim pq o plot realmente é muito insano e pesado. e o jeito que ele é desenrolado no final do filme faz tudo se conectar, tudo fazer sentido, o que aumentou o impacto do plot msm assim. Queria ter sido chocado por esse plot mas fiquei mais chocado por ter previsto ele de cagada do que por ele mesmo. Ent, ⭐️⭐️⭐️.

exemplo: Vários espectadores ressaltam a forma como o filme aborda o impacto da guerra nas vidas das pessoas, com destaque para o sofrimento, o desespero e as consequências de longo prazo.
texto: Esta película muestra la perspectiva de una víctima que se ve afectada simplemente por ser ella misma, por buscar la verdad y no dejarse llevar por el odio aunque se ve “obligada “ a cambiar de pensamiento, Es una película que pone la lupa la geopolítica y sobre cómo los conflictos terminan afectando a personas que, como la protagonista, no los han elegido. El hilo de la historia no comienza porque ella haya hecho algo malo, sino porque, en muchas ocasiones, no somos nosotros quienes decidimos nuestras batallas desde el principio. Poco a poco, las circunstancias nos obligan a formar parte de ellas, cuando lo único que buscábamos era una vida estable, tranquila y poder creer en algo que realmente tuviera valor.

exemplo: A reviravolta é frequentemente citada como chocante e brutal, mesmo por quem diz ter previsto o desfecho; alguns a consideram desnecessária, mas a maioria a descreve como um golpe que reconfigura toda a narrativa.
texto: A guerra leva consigo tantas perdas, tantas memórias... E no final resta uma casca vazia, deixando-nos a opção de escolher entre se ferir com a verdade e preencher esse vacuo; ou esquece-la em meio a memória fragmentada. Esse aqui foi um soco no estômago completo. Nunca pensei que veria algo que se igualasse a Oldboy, mas aparentemente Incendies existe pra me mostrar que eu estava errado.

Filmin Lübnan'ın yetmişlerinde yaşadığı mezhep çatışmalarını yansıttığını dilin kullanımı ve olaylar bağlamında anlayabiliyoruz. sinematografide ise çağdaşı yönetmenlerin aksine gerçekliği sarı filtresiz, oryantalizmden uzak, donuk bir şekilde anlatması özellikle beni memnun etti. hikayeye gelirsek filmi en başından itibaren ağlayarak izledim. insan geçmişinden ne kadar uzağa gitse, ne ölçüde kaçabilir? farklı mekanlarda kendimize farklı kimlikler inşa ediyoruz, peki bizi biz yapan acılardan kendimizi ne ölçüde arındırabiliriz? bu soruları düşünerek izledim filmi. en sondaki plot twist pornosu bence çok gereksizdi, hikayenin geri kalanı zaten halihazırda içimizi ezen - ama gerçekleşmiş olması kuvvetle muhtemel - olaylar bütünüyken, sondaki o meşhur sahnenin varlığı sadece midemi kaldırdı.

texto: beh, diciamo uno dei racconti più emozionanti, profondi e meglio riusciti di sempre? si potrebbe. questo film racconta semplicemente come da trama, la storia di due figli, canadesi, che devono ricercare la proprie origini per volere della defunta madre, nel medio oriente. ma quello che narra il film semplicemente è un viaggio intrecciato con l'amore familiare, le atrocità della guerra e il disperato bisogno di sapere, sapere la verità sui propri cari. cioè sinceramente è abbastanza sconvolgente, riesce per tutto il film a essere e rimanere così costantemente appunto, disarmante perchè sia nelle scene di guerra, di fuga o anche solo di dialogo, si sente proprio tutto l'orrore dei personaggi che soffrono e lottano fino allo sfinimento contro tutti e tutto. poi c'è sicuramente una grande fotografia da parte di villnueve che usa benissimo il grande panorama medio-orientale per farci capire che purtroppo a volte il mondo, sceglie il destino per alcune persone come la madre dei due figli, che non ha potuto scegliere dettata sia dall'amore che dal terrore. assurdo, molto anche profondo, per i temi religiosi, etnici e familiari ecco tutto gira lì, perché tutto diventa molto più personale quando si tocca la famiglia.

texto: Wow, I really don’t know what to say. Villeneuve is easily one of my favorite directors, and he creates such an expertly crafted story of family, war, and grief. The landscapes and visuals pull everything together so well, with static and lingering shots that really make you feel the emptiness and harshness of the world. It takes you through a multigenerational story, slowly unwinding the truth behind so much mystery. The first hour broke me, and I was out of tears for a while, but I assure you I would’ve had more if possible. Radiohead being the only songs in this is kinda hilarious, but it also works. As soon as the first song began I instantly recognized it and thought, “how does Denis have the audacity to play this after what just occurred.” It’s such a gruesomely real look into the world of war and how that shapes people. The narrative structure and time jumps, combined with the immense amount of travel, also help show the determination and desperation the characters have. It always gives you enough to understand and feel what’s happening without overloading you or cutting anything short. I do think the third act loses some momentum, and the ending itself is really emotionally deep but also a bit too coincidental and almost feels forced for impact. However, that really didn’t take away from the experience of watching this. It’s truly incredible and definitely something I have to rewatch. Wouldn’t be shocked if it rises to a 4.5 or even a 5.

texto: Day 1 of surviving my bsf favorite movies @ruyaarchive… I understand what this movie is trying to say. I understand the biblical allegory, the symbolism of Mother Nature, creation, worship, humanity, destruction, the cycle of creation and destruction, and all of that. I genuinely do. But understanding what a movie is trying to communicate doesn’t mean I have to enjoy watching it. Because honestly, for most of this movie, all I could think was: why the fuck is this man incapable of respecting his wife’s boundaries? From the very beginning, Mother is uncomfortable with these people invading her home. This is their house. Her safe space. The place she has been rebuilding and caring for. Yet Him constantly welcomes more and more people inside because he enjoys being admired. He doesn’t care that she’s uncomfortable. He doesn’t care that her privacy is being invaded. He doesn’t care that the people he’s invited are destroying the very home she has worked so hard to create. And that was the most frustrating part of the entire movie for me. I didn’t see some mysterious, fascinating, all-powerful Creator. I saw an incredibly self-absorbed man who desperately needs to be worshipped and praised by everyone around him, to the point where he is willing to sacrifice the person closest to him for it. And then the movie just keeps escalating. The guests become increasingly obsessive. The worship becomes increasingly disturbing. The house turns into complete chaos. And somehow, through all of this, Him continues to let them in. At some point I genuinely felt like I was watching a cult form around this man. People aren’t simply admiring him anymore—they’re worshipping him. They’re willing to destroy everything around them for him. And Mother? She is the one who actually creates. She is the one who gives life. She is the one who builds and nurtures. Yet she is ultimately valued for what she can provide, not for who she is. Her existence is treated as something useful because she can create life, while her own needs and boundaries are repeatedly ignored. The most disturbing thing to me is that the people who worship Him don’t even truly care about what they destroy. They can adore him while simultaneously destroying the very thing that makes his creation possible. And he allows it because their love and worship matter more to him than protecting Mother. Which brings me to the ending, where I just sat there thinking: What the actual fuck? Mother gives everything. She is destroyed. The house is destroyed. The cycle ends in complete devastation. And Him? He survives. He takes what remains and starts again. So we’re essentially watching a cycle where Mother is repeatedly created, used, worshipped only for what she can give, destroyed by the people who claim to love the Creator, and then replaced by another Mother so the cycle can continue. I understand that this is supposed to represent something much larger. I understand the biblical parallels. I understand the commentary on humanity, religion, creation, environmental destruction, and the endless cycle of worship and destruction. I still fucking hated it. I spent the entire movie waiting for someone to simply tell these people to leave the house. 😭 Maybe the allegory is brilliant. Maybe the symbolism is layered and intentional. Maybe there are dozens of things I could analyze about this movie. But as an actual viewing experience? I was miserable. I didn’t feel scared. I didn’t feel emotionally connected. I felt increasingly irritated at a man who couldn’t respect his wife’s privacy, increasingly uncomfortable watching a group of people turn into a cult around him, and increasingly horrified by the realization that nobody seemed to care about Mother as a person. One & half stars. I understand you, mother!. I just don’t like you. 💀

texto: Like some other Aronofsky films it may take an viewing to understand it better, though I will not do a second viewing, will read up on that ending especially, instead.  Despite all the cool attempts that symbolism, I think a lot of it just got too lost in the shock level graphic presentation of it. Love the ending song (but not this cover version - uncredited. I don't think that was Skeeter Davis singing it!) starting the credits. Interesting and top-level cast. Jennifer Lawrence does all the heavy lifting in the movie and does it very well, though so much of the film is quite the metaphorical shitshow. A couple of (previously unfamiliar to me) Gleeson Brothers snuck in there too. Interesting and perhaps a just little disturbing soundscape and live artwork drawing across the ending credits. Hang in there for this bonus effect - especially if you were into the movie.

texto: darren aronofsky is a brilliant director, but he’s far from a great writer. he’s at his absolute best when he’s adapting another’s work. Black Swan, The Wrestler, and Requiem for a Dream being perfect examples of that. not even sure why he would attempt to write a story like this. as a man myself this just seems undoable from my perspective; at least without being half baked or offensive. this was overly pretentious and not something that deserves attention as a “misunderstood masterpiece.” frankly, i find it hard to believe that anyone with decent media literacy would be unable to comprehend this. that climax is quite abysmal as well, knocked it down half a star for me. i do respect its moments of intensity though. also a lot of beautiful shots throughout.

exemplo: Muitos notaram que o ritmo é lento na primeira metade, mas a reta final se torna uma avalanche de violência e acontecimentos bizarros que quebram a tensão construída inicialmente.
texto: Aronofsky’s signature blend of terrifying, pretentious, and heavy symbolism gets me every time but this.... To give credit where it’s due, the allegories are sooo interesting, whether you view it as a critique of an artist's ego or a detailed allegory of the Bible (with the Husband as God, the guests as Adam and Eve making the crystal the forbidden fruit, the brothers' fight a Cain and Abel situation with the mark on the floor as Cain's mark). The frantic descent into chaos leading to the finale throws a harsh spotlight on societal collapse, throwing at thr audience brutal, inexplicable human crimes in rapid flashes without giving you a second to breathe. When it works, it’s dynamic and overwhelming. But all that madness in the final act couldn't rescue the fuuucking slow burn of the first half. The early narrative drags so much that it completely lost my interest. A brilliant concept wrapped in a disappointing viewing experience which is a shame cause I really had my hopes up..

texto: Je trouve ça dommage de faire un huis clos pour y mettre tous les éléments de l'extérieur tels qu'ils sont. Par exemple une manif, la guerre, la police ? Dans une maison ? J'ai adoré la première partie, la tension est extrêmement forte, la mise en scène est vraiment plaisante, il y a un vrai jeu entre des plans très serrés et des plans en pdv subjectif plus larges. Ça donne une impression de voyeurisme, comme si la femme et la maison était la même personne (ce qui est le but). Ensuite il y a les premiers invités (la famille nucléaire), cette tension continue et en même temps des mystères se développent : qui sont ils ? Que se passe-t-il au sous sol ? Que signifie cette pierre ? Qu'écrit le mari ? C'est oppressant, on ne sait rien et tous les éléments sont stressants. À partir de ce moment là c'est très bien, les symboliques sont délicates, complètes et ça garde une forte puissance de propos. Personnellement j'y ai d'abord vu une idée féministe, la femme fait un travail monstrueux de rénovation pour que l'homme ait tout le buzz en écrivant (alors même qu'il écrit pas). Ensuite arrivent tout le reste de la famille, ça continue d'être stressant mais ça en devient ironique. C'est à dire qu'avant on savait que ça pouvait déraper puisqu'il y a avait un petit groupe d'intrus, mais là avec un groupe de 20 personnes, toutes différentes, la seule peur qui reste c'est la gêne qu'on ressent face à leurs comportements. Après que tout cela se calme, on revient sur du bon contenu : la relation dans le couple. Puis suite à la révélation de la grossesse et la fin de l'écriture, tout repars en couilles. Mais cette fois si c'est pire puisque plus rien n'a de symbolique. L'intérêt du début c'est surtout qu'il y a une symbolique cachée qui est la genèse de la bible. Mais passé cette étape là, on se lance dans une critique du christianisme d'une manière grossière. Pourquoi ne pas continuer le jeu de la symbolique ? Pourquoi faire des évènements aussi burlesques ? C'est vraiment de plus en plus grossier, tout ça pour avoir une critique très mid style "ah ouais la bible dit de tout partager, d'être gentil avec son prochain mais les gens ils sont pas gentils boubouuh 😣"  ou sinon une critique un peu incompréhensible qui est que Dieu ce flocko il veut trop la fame. Mouais à revoir. En plus le propos féministe que j'ai expliqué avant est bien estompé puisque ce n'est pas vraiment la femme qui charbonne (dans les 2 sens du terme) mais c'est Dieu qui crée Marie (la maison) comme hôte afin d'accueillir Jésus pendant qu'il écrit. C'est à dire qu'elle ne travaille pas vrm, c'est elle la maison et elle se prépare juste à son rôle premier : accoucher de l'autre pelo à l'auréole. Au global, le film avait un potentiel de fou, mais on ne sait pourquoi c'est passé du thriller horrifique à du comique.

texto: Very disturbing introduction to Aronofsky. This had a really strong first hour, that for me tapered off as it progressed. The atmosphere was well done, sort of established a dream-like state that made the bizarre escalation of events not seem too far fetched. Mostly felt like this was done through all of the characters interactions being very distant to mother, with an emphasis on her husband. Nobody’s really responding or registering with her actual dialogue - really isolated Lawrence as the only grounded character, super terrifying when taking into account the husband is her only lifeline in the setting and he quickly shows he is not reliable. This, as well these long panning shots of mother claustrophobically close to the camera attempting to maneuver her home (in which continuity seems to only apply where she is present) make it super nightmarish. Was super off trying to analyze this movie, first half felt more like a psyche thriller and I thought these visiting characters were representing all aspects of doubt in her life, like the man challenging her autonomy over the home and decision making while the women challenges her adequacy as a wife and potential mother - the sons would just be some internal violence I guess? Came around to the biblical allegory thing but I think my original outlook tainted the way the rest of the film panned out. Solid overall.

texto: Uma das obras mais densas que eu já vi. Tal qual experimentar um prato que de tão spicy deixa a sua boca adormecida, e mesmo assim você curte a experiência, Mother não é filme pra você sair tranquilo, é pesado, espesso, um turbilhão que te deixa cansado. Eu pessoalmente nunca fui masoquista que gosta de sofrer com algo que era pra me trazer júbilo, mas Darren Aronofsky acaba por me fazer senti prazer em ver algo pertubador. Caim, Abel, Adão, Eva, Cristo, Mãe, A humanidade, todos esses são muito bem retratados, mas estão simplesmente ofuscador por Javier Bardem, um ególatra maluco que interpreta Deus, só fica a pergunta de: como ele consegue ser tão perfeito na própria visão, e mesmo assim ser a pior coisa da existência?

This one had me go through many emotions and at the same time, left me feeling used and hollow…truly trained but so fucking mad at the same time. Incredible. That desperate need to be loved and giving your all to one person just for them to use you to fill the void. People just take and take, ignoring your boundaries, your wishes, your humanity, all to fulfill their own desperate need to feel loved and admired. The more she gives, the more she was expected to give, until there's nothing left of her. And the cruelest part was that it was all for a man who never truly saw her never truly loved her…A FUCKING MAN. Also lets take a moment for Jennifer Lawrences performance in this, chefs kiss.

texto: Recordé mucho el cuento Casa Tomada de Julio Cortázar , intrusos que entran a tu casa sin invitación y mi interpretación es que e todos estos entes son los monstruos e inseguridades en la cabeza de él. Su deseo por la fama, el reconocimiento, su incapacidad de conectar incluso con su propia poesía, todo eso que jamás le funcione una relación. Inicialmente el suspenso fue creado por las actuaciones, la primera hora es una secuencia de incomodidad y espera pero el horror se logra en los últimos 30 min. La tomé como una película pretenciosa hasta que entiendes la metáfora en los últimos minutos, me parece que es una analogía lo que un depredador hace, succionar la energía de mujeres que le sirvan, no reaccionen ni cuestionen y si no lo cumplen, lo desechan porque habrá otra mujer dispuesta a ser elegida. Me encanta que el título sea mother! porque muchas veces las mujeres somos reducidas a ser madres en un matrimonio y en la sociedad. exemplo: As cenas de batalha são apontadas como visualmente impressionantes, mas carecem de estratégia e tática, sendo muitas vezes confusas e sem o brilhantismo militar que caracterizou Napoleão.
texto: the track ‘dawn’ from pride and prejudice is played over the scene where josephine flashes napoleon so that was quite an experience for me i’m quite disappointed by the battles, i mean austerlitz was napoleon’s masterpiece and it barely got any screen time (and leipzig got nothing!) and waterloo…the funniest thing was when a rifleman said ‘i have bonaparte in my sights, should i shoot?’ as if firstly the french and english command tents were that close together and secondly as if you could make that shot with a baker rifle 😭 also the french having no idea what to do with square formation- where are your cannons napoleon? the entire battle was just wrong no french column advance, napoleon RIDING INTO BATTLE???, wellington commentating like its a football match what a joke there are a lot more inaccuracies, but, putting those aside, this film was boring and slow and focused far too much on bonaparte’s romantic entanglements and (inaccurately detailed) statecraft rather than his military genius and tactical brilliance and i recommend anyone who wants to watch an actual napoleonic film to watch waterloo (1970) regrettably watched the directors cut ._.

tema: Foco excessivo na relação com Joséphine
exemplo: Muitas avaliações reclamam que o filme dedica muito tempo à relação entre Napoleão e sua esposa, em detrimento de sua trajetória militar e política.
texto: Ce film aurait pu traiter des sujets passionnants : les stratégies de combat de Napoléon, sa manière d'être et de commander durant la guerre, ce qu'il cherchait réellement à obtenir. Au lieu de ça, le film se concentre presque exclusivement sur sa relation avec Joséphine, du début à la fin un choix assez insupportable, étant donné que cette relation est montrée de façon plate. Cela dit, de mémoire, le film reste visuellement correct, sans plus. La bande-son, en revanche, est vraiment réussie.

Joaquin has done better work for sure.

texto: Długo wzbraniałem się przed nadrobieniem "Napoleona". Najlepsze lata Ridleya Scotta już dawno przeminęły, a w międzyczasie trudno było uniknąć opinii, że nie do końca ten film zasłużonemu reżyserowi wyszedł, ale mimo wszystko podszedłem do niego z czystą głową. Początek wzniecił sporo nadziei swoimi przedstawionymi w sposób imponujący i brutalny scenami batalistycznymi, które poziomu nie obniżyły już do samego końca i były najjaśniejszym punktem filmu. Co zaś momentalnie stanęło w kontrze do pozytywów to sam pomysł na przedstawienie głównego bohatera, gdzie Scott nie potrafił się zdecydować czy chce ukazać go w sposób karykaturalny, czy też jako pomysłowego i brutalnego przywódcę. Na tym przede wszystkim ucierpiał, pomimo swojego kunsztu aktorskiego, Joaquin Phoenix. Generalnie można stwierdzić, że twórcy nie do końca zapanowali nad tą produkcją, bo kilka dziwnych i niezrozumiałych zabiegów można znaleźć również w montażu. Co jednak najbardziej kłuje w oczy, to to jak poszatkowana i pozbawiona jakiejkolwiek ciągłości jest tu fabuła. Przez większość czasu nic się tutaj nie spina, a widz zamiast starannie opowiedzianej historii, dostaje zbiór najważniejszych momentów z życia Bonaparte. Żeby nie kończyć swoich przemyśleń tak ponuro, dodam że Vanessa Kirby świetnie się odnalazła w roli Józefiny. Szkoda, bo był potencjał.

Les inexactitudes historiques ne sont pas si dérangeantes étant donné que le film est centré sur la personne de Napoléon, presque de manière parodique, bien que j’aurai préféré avoir un film le plus juste que possible. Joaquin Phenix est très loin du niveau qu’il pouvait avoir dans le rôle du Joker, par exemple. Il y a un décalage conséquent entre le nain colérique pour lequel passe Napoléon tout au long du film et la fin romancée au maximum avec ses soi-disant dernières paroles. Cette transition ne colle pas du tout avec l’atmosphère que dégage le film, il aurait mieux fallu se concentrer sur un seul aspect de Napoléon et de tirer son potentiel jusqu’au bout, ici le film paraît informe. Le budget qui a été investi n’est absolument pas justifier.

texto: Como diría el grandísimo PEPO FANTASY: “en plan… se centran demasiado en lo que es el amor con la jamba”. Me da realmente pena no haber caído de pie viendo ‘Napoleon’ y que no haya conseguido embaucarme en su viaje por la vida del gobernante corso más allá de por la calidad y espectacularidad de las escenas bélicas que son por lo que realmente sí que merece la pena ver esta película en el cine. Una decepción más de mi queridísimo Ridley Scott que vuelve a traer una película visual y sonoramente muy llamativa pero que deja que desear en cuanto a trama y personajes (sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que no es un personaje cualquiera si no una de las personas más influyentes de la historia). Y a esto hay que sumarle que la decepción que te llevas es doble cuando vas a ver una película con un director como este y que protagoniza ni mas ni menos que the one and only Joaquin Phoenix. Sin poder (obviamente) definir su actuación como mala o mediocre, hay algo en ella que no me ha convencido, sin saber realmente si ha sido por la actuación en sí o por la cantidad de grandes papeles que asocio a este actor y que por ello me cueste más verle en la piel de un personaje tan tan conocido. Una trama repleta de saltos y que, pese a narrar todos los hechos importantes de la vida de Napoleón, lo hace de una forma que en ciertos momentos es capaz de sacarme de la película por su velocidad para pasar de unos sucesos a otros, por la ausencia de elementos clave (Trafalgar) y por el, para mi gusto, exceso de trama dedicada al amor; aunque la actuación de Vanessa Kirby sea bastante bastante GOAT.

texto: Une bande annonce qui promettait un Ridley Scott au plus haut de sa forme avec un nouveau film historique mémorable et c’est assez décevant. Dans les points positifs : Joaquin Phoenix et Vanessa Kirby, de beaux plans et de bonnes scènes ainsi qu’une photographie magnifique. Le point negatif est son histoire qui se concentre sur la partie la moins interessante du recit c’est a dire l’histoire d’amour entre Nzpoleon et Josephine. On skip beaucoup trop de moments très important comme la montée de Napoleon, son sacre qui expusé en 5min et la bataille de Moscou. Ma note : 6/10 22-11-23

texto: Al ser una pelicula sobre la historia de Nápoleon le tenía una gran expectativa pero me decepcionó un montón por las carencias que tuvo por todos lados. Para empezar no me podes poner a alguien conocido como intérprete de una figura histórica, en estas películas a mi gusto tenes que poner a un actor que no lo conozca ni su vieja incluso si eso implica bajar la calidad actoral, porque uno después cuando la ve, no está viendo a Napoleón, está viendo a Joaquín Phoenix y que te pase eso es que se te cague toda la película. En términos cinematográficos me pareció buena en las escenas de batallas, pero de las 4 que muestran 2 las mostraron en menos de 10 segundos entonces lo interesante que tiene te deja con gusto a poco, después el resto de las escenas me parecen básicas, no creo que Joaquín Phoenix le haya agregado mucha calidad o personalidad al personaje. Para lo que pudo haber hecho, que Ridley Scott haga esto es para que lo descarten en un río. Habiendo hablado de esas dos cosas, una de las mayores carencias de la película sino la mayor es el tiempo que se toman y el cómo retratan la relación de él con Josephine, habrá tomado sin exagerar mitad de las 2:30 que tiene la película y es lo que menos importa de toda su historia, aparte de que las escenas son cualquiera mal, no se hablo de un solo General que después de las batallas en sí, debe ser lo más relevante de contar: no profundizaron con Murat, no hablaron ni de Davout ni de Ney y más grave todavía no hablaron nada de Lannes, a Dumas lo mostraron forzado solo por ser su único general negro y lo hicieron con errores históricos como que era amigo medio íntimo cuando no era para nada el caso o que apareciera después de la campaña de Egipto cuando en realidad creo que ni había terminado esa campaña que ya se había retirado. La crítica de las campañas seguro debe ser la que más la habrán hecho y con razón, ya que es realmente increíble lo escaso que está en material de las campañas que es los más importante y lo único que debería tener en mente el director al hacer la película ya que justamente las campañas son lo que le dieron peso a su figura, hasta incluso más que las batallas de nombre aisladas. En la campaña de Italia mostraron la de Toulon por arriba y después nada más, en la de egypto no se mostró una sola  batalla ni siquiera lo que pasó cuando se exilio y dejó a Kleber. Mas adelante se pueden saltear alguna que otra batalla pero siempre y cuando se mantenga el hilo de la historia, cosa que no pasó, el que no pispeo la historia antes de verla no hay forma de que se ubique porque no se entiende nada. Siguiendo con lo de antes ponele que se vieron las batallas más importantes pero incluso ahi hay carencias porque como no me vas a poner la puta batalla de Marengo o la de Rivoli hermano, no se te pueden pasar esas nunca y mucho menos se te puede pasar nunca jamás en la vida la campaña esa que hizo cuando volvió del exilio. Tiempo mal utilizado, floja cinematografía, errores de história y muy incompleto en términos generales.

texto: Movie sure has its peaks, but it's too far away from being impressive. In the movie Napoleon's personality is mainly linked to his love story with Josephine, making him almost a toy for her. I liked certain characters like Tzar Alexander and Wellington, but many things weren't historically precise at all. Napoleon didn't flee from Egypt because of Josephine and, when he escaped from Elba, she was already dead. They didn't represent the man who was able to put almost all of Europe to his feet.

texto: The year is 2023, and two new biopics have been released about some of the most destructive men known to our world. One of those films is named Oppenheimer, and it clocks in at roughly three hours and one minute. The other film is named Napoleon, and it clocks in at roughly two hours and thirty-eight minutes. Now ask yourself: Which film is longer? If you answered Oppenheimer, then you haven’t watched both films. After a rewatch the film decidedly conveys its points a lot better, and it’s a decent biopic that separates the man from the myth. That being said, decent is the word for it, because half of the time either Joaquin’s acting is meandering and aimless or Napoleon’s mood is being written to abruptly shift contradictory to how he should be acting. The one highlight of Napoleon’s writing is it at least shows the slow degradation of the main character’s mannerisms as they get overtaken by ambition. For anyone wondering, yes I have watched Oppenheimer before and yes at some point I will rewatch it and rate it accordingly. texto: This cut is so much better than the original. While I was planning to save Ridley Scott’s Napoleon until I reached the next chapter of my director deep dive, the opportunity arose to watch it, so I took it. At three and a half hours, Scott’s director’s cut is a substantial expansion of the theatrical version. It doesn’t quite add the sense of scale I expected from an extra hour of runtime, but that’s easy to forgive when the film delivers on the level that it does. Napoleon certainly has its flaws, and some of them are significant, but in the grand scheme of things, it’s a great time. From the opening sequence, the film radiates a grit that seems to seep off the screen, steadily building throughout the runtime. That escalation culminates in several disturbing scenes of political violence that are incredibly effective. Scott captures the messiness of government, revolution, and monarchy with remarkable clarity, making it easy to understand the absolute chaos of France’s political climate during this period. The director’s cut is far more expansive and patient with its pacing, allowing these elements to breathe and making the atmosphere all the more effective. Much of that atmosphere is still rooted in the relationship between Josephine and Napoleon, just as it was in the original cut. What elevates it here are the expanded plotlines surrounding Napoleon’s rise to power, along with the greater focus given to key political and historical developments. These additions provide the film with far more depth and substance than its theatrical counterpart. My biggest issue with the film, both the director’s cut and the theatrical version, is its use of American accents in place of French ones. It’s a truly baffling decision that repeatedly pulls the viewer out of the film’s otherwise immersive atmosphere. It feels especially strange when you have a Russian character speaking with a Russian accent while a native Frenchman speaks with an American one. It constantly distracted me. I understand why Joaquin Phoenix was cast, he is excellent and perfectly suited to the role in many ways. However, I can’t understand why he doesn’t attempt a French accent at all. While his star power undoubtedly helped the film commercially, the decision to forgo an accent altogether may have avoided certain pitfalls, but it ultimately hurts the film’s authenticity and integrity.

It’s a truly baffling decision that repeatedly pulls the viewer out of the film’s otherwise immersive atmosphere. It feels especially strange when you have a Russian character speaking with a Russian accent while a native Frenchman speaks with an American one. It constantly distracted me. I understand why Joaquin Phoenix was cast, he is excellent and perfectly suited to the role in many ways. However, I can’t understand why he doesn’t attempt a French accent at all. While his star power undoubtedly helped the film commercially, the decision to forgo an accent altogether may have avoided certain pitfalls, but it ultimately hurts the film’s authenticity and integrity.

texto: I've always thought that making a film about a great historical figure is one of the hardest things a director can do. Unless it's a TV series or a whole film saga, trying to fit an entire life into a single movie means leaving out a lot of important moments. And when that person is Napoleon Bonaparte—a man whose life was defined by politics, military genius, and an incredibly complex personality—the challenge becomes even greater. Any filmmaker has to balance historical accuracy with cinematic spectacle, and I think Ridley Scott only partially succeeds. The film follows the major milestones of Napoleon's life in chronological order and recreates some of his most famous campaigns. At the same time, it takes several dramatic liberties to make them more visually impressive. The cannon fire aimed at the Pyramids never happened, Napoleon wasn't present at Marie Antoinette's execution, and the famous frozen lake sequence at Austerlitz is a huge exaggeration of what actually took place. Those scenes are entertaining, but they prioritize spectacle over history. Honestly, those changes don't bother me that much because they're based on real events that have simply been dramatized. What I do miss are the omissions that make it harder to understand who Napoleon really was. The film barely touches on his background as a member of the Corsican minor nobility, something that was essential in allowing him to attend military school in France and begin the career that eventually led him to become Emperor. Joséphine also deserved a more nuanced portrayal. The movie mostly reduces her role to Napoleon's wife and his desperate need for an heir. While that was certainly an important part of their relationship, she was also a politically influential figure who navigated the highest circles of French society and played a significant role while Napoleon was away. The film turns a remarkably capable historical figure into little more than a romantic subplot. That said, I do think the movie succeeds in portraying Napoleon as more than just a military genius. We see an awkward, emotionally intense man whose love for Joséphine shapes much of his personal life. Joaquin Phoenix captures that contradiction between the vulnerable individual and the unstoppable conqueror surprisingly well. I also liked how the film hints at Napoleon's admiration for Julius Caesar and Alexander the Great. At times, Scott presents him as someone driven by an almost classical sense of duty—a man convinced that his destiny was to serve France above everything else. Whether intentional or not, that echoes the Roman ideal of devotion to the state and adds another layer to his character.

texto: I’ll preface by saying i only watched the director’s cut. That said, god, i hate that i liked this. Do i think it’s a good portrayal of how Napoleon was perceived by others? Perhaps not, but i do think it does a fantastic job in making you feel like how it would’ve been inside his mind throughout his life. Especially towards the end where failure was more and more common. The huge battles, sets, cavalry charges, all of it was a feast for the eyes. The actors did a good job, and i feel like Joaquin Phoenix and Vanessa Kirby were the quite obvious standouts. Although i must say i liked Edouard Philipponant portrayal of the tsar as well. It has a lot of flaws, as a film. But it’s enjoyable, and never boring which i see as the worst sin a film can commit. Made 3 hours and then some feel like an hour. Perhaps the last good Ridley Scott movie,  but of course i’d love to be proved wrong.

texto: Un deuxième visionnage bien rentable, cette fois-ci vu en version intégrale qui rajoute 48 minutes environ. Je me rappelle que la version cinéma de 2h40 donnait l'impression que les évènements s'enchaînaient bêtement et sans raison, ce qui n'est pas le cas dans la director's cut. Napoléon de Ridley Scott est indéniablement imparfait et inégal. La photographie est parfois sublime, parfois absolument infecte. Bien sûr, c'est plus souvent beau que laid... Mais je ne peux vraiment pas passer outre cette scène d'ouverture affreuse, qui annonce vraiment mal le film. Qu'est-ce que c'est moche pendant la première minute ! La musique aussi est pompeuse pendant une bonne heure avant de devenir bonne. Mais les scènes d'action sont particulièrement réussies : très belles, toutes uniques, on comprend bien ce qui s'y passe (pas comme dans un certain blockbuster récent que je ne citerai pas...), et durent globalement le temps qu'il faut. Il faut noter que le film s'essouffle un peu pendant la deuxième heure avant de repartir de plus belle. En terme de mise en scène, c'est à la fois subtil, maîtrisé, et parfois un poil grossier/burlesque, ce qui n'est pas nécessairement un défaut. Je pense que c'est le genre de films ou beaucoup de détails nous échappent et que l'on découvre au fur et à mesure des visionnages. Ensuite évidemment, là où le film ne prend pas tellement de risques en matière de costumes et de décors (ce qui me dérange un peu car la reconstitution historique ne m'intéresse franchement pas, et je n'aime pas tellement le style de cette époque), il en prend énormément sur le fond. Et cette prise de risque fondamentale, qui est de faire de Napoléon un personnage mauvais et comique, est géniale ! Elle porte franchement le film et lui donne un intérêt. Phoenix est excellent dans ce rôle (sous certains angles, la ressemblance avec le vrai Napoléon est frappante). L'idée de faire d'un Empereur que la tradition historique prend au sérieux un simple cocu immature en manque d'amour et qui a clairement des dizaines de manques à combler, c'est merveilleux. De quoi rendre fou tout morveux qui prétend être un patriote en adorant ce neuille de Napoléon. Qu'est-ce que je préfère un protagoniste de la sorte, absolument inattendu et presque dégoûtant, à un personnage historique qui répond simplement aux attentes d'un spectateur lambda qui s'attend à un film épique comme les autres, du style Pierre Niney dans le Comte de Monte-Cristo. Bien entendu, j'aime bien Pierre Niney malgré sa filmo douteuse, mais le comparer à Phoenix c'est comme comparer une panthère et un moustique. Aussi pour revenir sur le personnage de Napoléon, j'apprécie beaucoup l'idée d'en faire un mégalo matrixé par l'envie de devenir un des grands de l'histoire au point d'écrire sa propre histoire de son vivant. (Bien sûr Napoléon de la vraie vie était aussi quelqu'un d'intelligent, à l'origine de plusieurs avancées notables, un fin stratège etc... Ok, mais dans un film c'est pas intéressant de voir ça. Je considère également qu'une grande intuition n'empêche en rien qu'il fut une grosse merde humaine). Les deux motifs sur lesquels je devrai davantage me concentrer au prochain visionnage seront la possessivité de Napoléon à l'égard de Joséphine/La France, et la lumière céleste. Bref, un film imparfait mais pour lequel j'ai étonnement développé avec le temps une réelle tendresse. Inutile de préciser que tout ce qui est vérité ou crédibilité historique est pour moins un non-argument car il s'agit de fiction, et que Ridley Scott a bien raison de se torcher le cul avec les livres d'histoire.

texto: ★★★★☆ (8/10) Napoléon est un film que j'ai beaucoup apprécié. Les scènes de bataille sont spectaculaires, la mise en scène est magnifique et les décors donnent une véritable impression de grandeur. Visuellement, le film est très impressionnant et certaines séquences restent gravées en mémoire, notamment l'entrée de Napoléon dans Moscou ou les grandes batailles. Joaquin Phoenix livre une très bonne performance et l'ensemble du casting est convaincant. J'ai aussi aimé la façon dont le film montre les différentes facettes de Napoléon, aussi bien comme stratège que comme homme. Je comprends les critiques de certains historiens sur les libertés prises avec les faits et le fait que le personnage ne soit pas toujours représenté de manière fidèle. Mais en mettant de côté l'exactitude historique, cela reste un très bon film. Je l'ai avant tout regardé comme une œuvre de cinéma, et de ce point de vue, j'ai passé un excellent moment. Même s'il n'est pas parfait, Napoléon reste un film épique, porté par une réalisation ambitieuse, de superbes scènes de bataille et une excellente interprétation de Joaquin Phoenix. Un solide 8/10.

texto: Director’s Cut I have really mixed feelings on this. While I have to say this is an outstanding production with stellar cinematography, amazing set and costume design and superb sound. The biggest issue for me was its uneven tone which treated the war time events with a dramatic seriousness, while the parts that focused on Napoleon’s personal life felt satirical. I have no idea whether this was intentional or not but it really threw me off. I also wasn’t the biggest fan of Joaquin Phoenix in this role due to the conflicting tone but I think that’s mostly down to the script which felt like Ridley Scott wanted to present Napoleon as a fragile pathetic character who hid behind his tactical genius, but I just found it to be jarring with it feeling like two separate characters and Phoenix was way too old for the majority of this role. I have heard criticism about the plot being shallow with it feeling like it quickly jumps to and from major plot points. I didn’t really think it did that but I must only presume this is due to the extra depth added within the Directors Cut. The action sequences in this were excellent and really showed Ridley Scott at his best with hard hitting brutality and authentic choreography creating some of the best large scale battles I’ve seen. The ending was also phenomenal. Vanessa Kirby was fantastic as Josephine who played a key role in Napoleon’s story. But, there are a lot of characters in this and while I don’t think anyone was particularly bad no one really stood out to me. I did enjoy this film with the full 3 and half hours feeling generally well paced. For me it doesn’t do much wrong apart from as I said the weird tone surrounding Napoleon but unfortunately that is a big deal considering the whole film surrounds him. This could have been an absolutely incredible film. I would love to know if the awkward portrayal of Napoleon’s personal life was intentional and maybe inspired by England’s historical propaganda that did show him as weak and childish. I would like to watch this again one day knowing what to expect.

texto: ​"Não vejo na religião o mistério da Encarnação, mas o mistério da ordem social. A religião associa ao Céu uma ideia de igualdade que impede que os ricos sejam massacrados pelos pobres." Achei os figurinos, a ambientação, os atores e a história incríveis, mas, mesmo assim, sinto que faltou algo. ​Sempre vou odiar guerras, mas não tem como negar que as batalhas nessa época eram fodas. A artilharia se baseava em canhões e armas que demoravam 30 segundos para ser recarregadas manualmente, e a cavalaria não passava de homens em cima de cavalos com espadas. Outro ponto que acho incrível é a proporção de quantas pessoas participavam dessas batalhas; só de imaginar meio milhão de homens se matando por ideias, é algo absurdo. Os dois únicos erros cometidos por Napoleão foram invadir a Rússia e amar demais. Napoleao é um dos maiores exemplos da ​Wille zum Leben.

Oui il y a des errances historiques nombreuses, mais on ne regarde pas un film pour sa vérité historique, au contraire, il m'a poussé à chercher des infos sur napoléon et son entourage. Néanmoins, il reste une belle fresque historique qu'il faut voir.

The quality of this film went down with every second of runtime. Even the things I liked at first were ruined, such as the use of liminal spaces and uncomfortable camera angles. I do understand that the meaning of this movie is about the objectification of women and their bodies and how people will use women as commodities for their beauty, but this film does not deliver on that. If you want me to care more about that meaning, maybe write an actual interesting film, not whatever the hell this bullshit was.

texto: eu literalmente me forcei a terminar esse filme. eu entendo completamente a proposta e reconheço que ele tem uma crítica interessante sobre padrões de beleza, envelhecimento, pressão estética e a obsessão da sociedade por uma versão cada vez mais jovem e “perfeita” das mulheres. mas, pra mim, a forma como tudo isso foi desenvolvido acabou ficando muito batida. em vários momentos eu sentia que o filme estava praticamente gritando a própria mensagem em vez de confiar que eu conseguiria entender sozinha. e quanto mais avançava, mais eu tinha a sensação de que já sabia exatamente onde aquilo ia chegar. a ideia é boa, a estética é interessante e algumas cenas são realmente muito bem feitas, mas não consegui me envolver com a história o suficiente pra gostar. dito isso, preciso reconhecer uma coisa: margaret qualley é linda. talvez esse tenha sido o verdadeiro motivo pelo qual eu consegui chegar até o final. porque toda vez que eu pensava “não vou aguentar mais esse filme”, ela aparecia na tela e eu pensava “tá bom, vou continuar”. no geral, achei previsível, exagerado e muito mais interessado em chocar do que em realmente me surpreender. mas se a verdadeira substância fosse “margaret qualley aparecendo na tela”, eu provavelmente teria dado 5. (isso me faz pensar que talvez eu seja quem o filme tanto está criticando)

TOUTEFOIS : Je savais pas que j'avais lancé un porno 💀 j'ai vu plus de cul et de seins que dans toute ma vie je crois (éventuellement à ne pas regarder avec des enfants mais a part ça il est catégorisé "déconseillé aux -12ans" ^^) Le film au 2/3 prend une tournure GORE a vomir tout ses repas sur les 4 derniers jours... Ma petite âme sensible a trouvé les images insupportables a regarder 🤮🤮 La scénographie est plutôt cool.... Le reste est a chier... Je déconseille, SAUF : aux personnes légèrement dérangées qui aiment regarder du gore et du cul (mon pote a kiffé le film, il me fait peur maintenant 😖)

texto: To put things briefly, The Substance is a relatively sound film, although, it still comes with a fair share of issues. As films of this more thematic nature, and more broadly within the horror genre typically demand, you’re sort of supposed to just go with the plot, which I struggle with. It’s not necessarily poorly written, it’s just contrived, not implausibly, but I still feel the beats could’ve been better strung together. Speaking of themes, it touches primarily on our contemporary culture, our media, and on the treatment of women, particularly within the public sphere; although I do find that the film fails to boldly challenge our perception of these social facets, or issues. For example, the premise, alongside how the film is shot evidently wish to discuss the self-objectification of the individual, of which is intrinsically tied to social norms, and to capitalism; yet this is highly surface level, and largely visual, it isn't actually protested. Overall, it's quite straightforward in its messaging, quite literally infantilising a woman, and I don’t have any qualms with it, however, a bit of nuance, or development upon these themes would’ve made the piece a touch more grounding, connecting, perhaps it might’ve helped alleviate the disconnect created by the grotesque body horror. On that, yeah, uhm, the film excels in disgusting me, although, I expected as much and genuinely struggled to convince myself to watch it. More technically, I was pleased in that colour wasn’t shied away from, as is the case frequently in this genre, and in this era; and the camerawork was solid, if albeit a bit uninspired—I also found it notable that some shots were clearly added solely for the sake of evoking disgust, or discomfort, even if the details were irrelevant, most prominently in the opening scenes of the film.

texto: La serie Z que rezuma. Sobre pinchazos y borbotones. Ya lo escribió Baruch Spinoza en su momento: nadie sabe lo que puede un cuerpo. Transcurrida una hora, me planteo si lo que estoy viendo es una película falsamente subversiva que parte de una idea explícita (la crítica a la sobreexposición del cuerpo femenino en la era del consumo, convertido en producto de carnicería a causa de la tiranía de la belleza) y la lleva al paroxismo. Sin embargo, conforme el relato avanza nos vamos encontrando con una suerte de retorno del espectro de "El hombre elefante", de "Carrie", de "Alien" y de otras múltiples tradiciones del cine norteamericano. Es contundente y celebratoria en el rumbo que toma y también divertida, e incluye una jocosa referencia a "Vertigo".

texto: Horrifying, stylish and clearly true to its intentions, The Substance is probably not for most, but you can’t deny it does what it does well. Unapologetically over the top, unsettling, gut-renching and excessive. At times it felt like never ending stimulation which was often overwhelming. Its strong Sci-fi element is enhanced by interesting designs and is complimented by a very well fitting score and visual aesthetic. All male characters were either hedonistic pigs or lame simps, the latter pretty much always being intolerable, though to its credit added to the unpleasantness of the world. Hyper-sexualisation served its underlying messages and aesthetic, however for me was excessive, although this perspective somewhat changed when I realised how exaggerated the rest movie was also. Denis Quade killed it. While I won’t be watching again, fans of body horror will surely be pleased, as this one takes the genre to new places in the craziest of ways. Well done, Coralie!

texto: Un peu tiraillée pour le coup, il y a beaucoup de choses que j'ai aimé mais aussi beaucoup de points qui m'ont dérangé Dans le positif, j'applaudis le cast que j'ai trouvé parfait, j'aime la mise en scène (surtout dans la première partie), scène de fin très fun et certains plans que j'ai trouvé magiques (je retiens surtout ce plan sur Demi Moore, portant une robe dos nue, assise au bar) Dans le négatif maintenant : - J'ai trouvé le film un peu trop répétitif par moment, j'avais parfois l'impression que le film poussait des scènes de façon grossières par peur que le spectateur ne comprenne pas le message (mais tqt vraiment on comprend) - Troooop de scènes sur les fesses de Margarett, je t'adore mais ça ajoute de nouveau de la longeur inutile et un côté redondant et puis surtout ça vient presque contredire le message du film - C'est pas un film féministe et c'est bon ca commence à fatiguer de présenter tous les films réalisés par des femmes comme ça. C'est pas la faute de la réal bien sûr, mais le message pseudo féministe n'aide pas malheureusement... Compétition officielle

texto: SFF2024 #7 (Closing Night Film) Spends a surprising amount of its third act riffing on extremely specific images from a not very well-regarded Doctor Who episode. This gets a lot of mileage out of its excellent concept, which allows for both lots of squeamishly fun body horror and plenty of (definitely unsubtle but undeniably worthwhile) social commentary about how we view women’s bodies culturally & the speed at which we tend to discard those on our screens once they reach a certain age. To her credit, Fargeat handles the topic deftly without resorting to the self-seriousness that trips up many a horror movie that sets out to say something about a specific issue, though I did feel at times that the film’s camp tone was keeping me at a slight ironic distance from the emotions of the characters. Said characters are brought to life nicely by the cast, though. I don’t think this is quite as much of a Demi Moore showcase as some of the Cannes critics hailed it as (by plot necessity, she’s off-screen for large chunks of the runtime), but it’s certainly bold, electric work from her. There’s a sequence where her character is overcome by body image-related insecurities while getting ready to go out, and it’s made as viscerally heartbreaking as it is by Moore’s excellent work. Margaret Qualley’s material is a bit more one-note but, as usual, she sells it on her screen presence alone (also, at the risk of proving the movie’s point, it must be said that she is quite hot). Dennis Quaid’s turn would be way too much in almost any other movie but it works for this one’s camp sledgehammer of an approach. Fargeat’s cooking with all the right ingredients here, but I think she undercuts herself with self-indulgence. There’s no real reason for this to be 140 minutes long; the concept could have easily made for a brilliant, punchy 90-minutes. By the third act, the movie just keeps piling hats onto hats in service of a gorefest that strays too far from the original allegory. It’s not that it isn’t a natural escalation of the conflict, per se, but I think it’s possible to escalate things a little too much, to the point where it becomes more numbing than impactful. There were several great possible endings in the climax, but Fargeat just kept dragging it out for no apparent reason, and the whole movie - while never boring - is similarly just a bit flabby given the simplicity of its plot. The film’s issues are not big enough to entirely sink it, but they definitely made me feel a bit out of step with the hype from Cannes. As recent Cannes-awarded, women-directed body horrors go, I’m much more of a Titane man.

texto: 5 stars for the cinematic experience that came with this movie. Without an audience I would have turned this off at the first transitioning scene. Filled with gore, horror, horniness and comedy The Substance was a lot - hence someone in the audience throwing up and fainting in the first 5 minutes of the film which should be taken as a compliment in this shocking genre. A great focus on existentialism and body dysmorphia for women all in hopes to please the embodiment of the rich touchy straight white male - the producer at a sexualised fitness TV program appropriately named Harvey (nice one). Many odes to other films such as The Shining and Trainspotting. Incredibly shot and well acted, I just don’t think this genre is for me. My jaw was on the floor and my ass cheeks were clenched, many sighs of relief when this came to an end.

texto: honestly loved how everything is shoved into your face via visual presentation and cues. some might criticize how this film exaggerates the message, slapping it on you with direct transparency as if it isn’t obvious enough, but in a world full of films buried in subtext, it’s refreshing to see one that makes the message painfully clear—especially since men (both as individuals and as a system) still don’t systematically grasp how physically, socially, and mentally detrimental beauty standards are for women. SO HELL YEAH, SHOVE THE MESSAGE UP THEIR ASSES. even the male looksmaxxing culture is just the tip of the iceberg compared to women's trenches. the dynamic between demi and margaret is excellent, and i cannot stress enough how good the casting is. demi’s performance evoked so much empathy in me, especially in her self‑destructive moments and when she tried to bring sue back, which eventually led to her gory death. elisa’s childhood friend really stood out to me, as he's such a symbolic figure or reminder of her potential recovery and self‑acceptance, though we all knew how their date would end. i definitely caught the significance of the final act, but it didn’t stand out because it felt comical. technically, everything is excellent, but again, monstra elisasue comes across as more comical than anything. i may or may not have missed the subtext if that was intentional. ultimately, all i can say is i fucking love depictions of female insecurities and frustrations with mirrors as cinematic tools.

exemplo: As reviews positivas apontam o filme como uma forte alegoria sobre como a obsessão pela juventude e pela aceitação pode levar à autodestruição, refletindo a pressão social sobre as mulheres.
texto: La película te deja un mensaje, esta película tiene muchísimas metáforas hacia dismorfia corporal, el odio a uno mismo y la adición, de como los comentarios de las personas te pueden hacer dudar de ti mismo hasta el punto de convertirte en una persona que haría lo que sea por agradar al otro, para sentirte “bien contigo mismo” pero en realidad solo te estás consumiendo por dentro, también el hecho de no querer envejecer y siempre lucir joven es un miedo que muchos adolescentes tenemos y está reflejado en esta película. Para los que no prestaron suficiente atención o no analizan las películas y los transfondos que pueden tener esta película seguramente que parecería bizarra o sin sentido pero hay que pararse a pensar y ver que en realidad te deja un mensaje. Me gustó la película.
